highlights.title: Microsoft issues emergency Windows 11 update to fix its record-breaking patch
highlights.summary: Microsoft has started rolling out an emergency out-of-band update to fix problems with its record-breaking September patch Tuesday update. The software giant patched nearly 1,000 flaws in its biggest update ever this month, but it also introduced some bugs that have affected businesses, developers…
body: The September patch Tuesday affected folder shares on Hyper-V-based Linux virtual machines, Remote Desktop Services sessions, and some USB audio devices. Microsoft’s out-of-band update, released yesterday, addresses these issues across Windows 11 versions 26h1, 25H2, and 24H2. Microsoft has also released updates for Windows Server 2025 and 2022, the LTSC versions of Windows 10, and Windows Server 2012 and Windows Server 2012 R2.

In the past it was unusual for Microsoft to issue out-of-band updates to Windows, but it has become far more common this year. In January the company was forced to issue four out-of-band updates after a buggy Windows 11 patch. In March the company then had to issue two emergency updates because of installation failures and Microsoft account sign-in problems. Microsoft also released an out-of-band update in July to address an Intel driver issue that was causing performance issues and battery drain.

highlights.title: Is Big Tech’s AI slowdown a safety pact or a cartel?
highlights.summary: When OpenAI CEO Sam Altman, Anthropic CEO Dario Amodei, Google DeepMind cofounder Demis Hassabis, and SpaceX head Elon Musk loosely agreed over the weekend to slow down AI development, skeptics spotted an ulterior motive immediately.
body: Major AI companies want to ‘pace the frontier’ — but their proposed solutions need real teeth.

The truth is more complicated, according to sources across the industry. The three-step proposal, laid out in an essay by Amodei, is calling for changes long espoused by AI safety advocates. While it could become a substitute for regulation, under Trump, substantial regulation is unlikely anyway. But experts say that on an issue that’s only likely to grow in importance, AI leaders aren’t the best people to lead the charge.

“The industry as a whole needs new champions,” said Nick Reese, an adjunct professor at New York University and the Department of Homeland Security’s former director of emerging tech policy. “We’ve looked at people like Dario Amodei, Sam Altman, and Elon Musk as these people who are closest to the problem and working on it every day, and they’re the ones who know best. But the truth is there’s never been a realistic vision for what we’re building toward.”
points: Major AI companies want to ‘pace the frontier’ — but their proposed solutions need real teeth.

highlights.title: Injustice 3 is seemingly the mysterious, unannounced fighting game that's been hosting playtests in California
highlights.summary: NetherRealm's next project has yet to be officially announced, but many believe it to be the third entry in the studio's superhero fighting game series Injustice. Now, there are new signs that select few outside the studio are playing Injustice 3.
body: This all started with a post on Good Gamer Group, a company that provides NDA-protected testing services for game publishers. The post, since been deleted, was spotted by EventHubs (via Kotaku ), which highlighted a number of curious pieces of evidence that all point to it being a NetherRealm project.

For starters, the listing includes two descriptors for the mystery game. It calls it a "triple-A fighting game" in one instance, and a "major 2D fighting game" in another. Neither is specifically limited to NetherRealm projects, of course, but as EventHubs points out, all the fighting games we know to be in the works are either smaller games or 3D fighters.

The location of the playtest is what gives us another clue. The playtest is held in Culver City, California, meaning the game is from an American studio. What's more, NetherRealm's parent company Warner Bros. Games also happens to be headquartered in the same city.

highlights.title: The pest I’ll never forget: the rat who jumped off the wardrobe and flew at my face
highlights.summary: There was a rat army in my flatshare, gnawing through pipes, carpets and even a bedroom door. That’s not to mention the mice... We should have known we were in trouble when we saw that the garden of our new place backed on to a Chinese restaurant in Hackney, London, with terrible reviews.
body: There was no stopping them. After sniffing out the remnants of an old snack in my housemate Simon’s bin, a pack of rats got to work one night gnawing through the wood at the bottom of his bedroom door. Like a rodent military exercise, they spent eight hours whittling a hole large enough to get through. I lay next door, 100% freaked out, panicking they’d try to get into my room next. I didn’t sleep a wink. Fairly soon after this, one of the rats died under the floorboards so we got a bottle-fly infestation to boot. Naturally, our landlord did nothing about any of this.

We tried not to kill them – in fact, Simon the pacifist locked a bunch in the saucepan cupboard using a wooden spoon. One day, he and I trapped one in his bedroom with us. It tried to get away from us by climbing to the top of the wardrobe. Suddenly, it jumped, body splayed, and flew at my face, ran down the entire length of my body and scuttled over my feet. Jonathan, our other housemate, walloped my toes with the metal pole, mistaking me for the rat.

highlights.title: What execs and politicians are saying about slowing down AI development
highlights.summary: Dario Amodei kicked off a flood of statements over the past few days about AI safety by publishing a long essay titled "We Must Pace the Frontier" detailing why AI development should be slowed down.
body: Dario Amodei kicked off a flood of statements about AI safety after publishing a long essay, with Sam Altman, President Trump, and others speaking out.

Amodei’s Saturday morning essay outlined three steps for pacing AI development: embedded third-party evaluators that can verify if a company is adhering to safety practices and commitments and report incidents, coordination between frontier AI companies in democratic countries on standards and limits, and global coordination between democratic governments and authoritarian governments on pacing AI development “to the extent this is possible.” Amodei said Anthropic is “unilaterally committing to the first of these steps.”

However, Amodei noted that pacing “does not mean halting model training or technical progress, ensuring companies take adequate time to align and safeguard their models, and for third party evaluators to confirm this.”

“I agree with Dario that we need to pace the frontier,” Altman said shortly after Amodei posted about his essay on X. “This has been a primary topic of discussions we’ve had at OpenAI in recent weeks.” Altman also committed to having independent evaluators at the company, calling it a “great idea.”

highlights.title: AI safety requires more than just slowing our pace | Stuart Russell
highlights.summary: Safety requirements are non-negotiable. They depend on meeting concrete goals, not just adjusting a timeline. It has been a week of high drama in AI, precipitated by the resignation of the AI safety researcher Jacob Coxon from Anthropic.
body: My inbox yesterday included a message from Business Insider with the subject line: “AI doomsday debate reaches boiling point”.

Now, the Anthropic CEO, Dario Amodei, has written a 3,800-word, reassuringly phrased letter titled “We Must Pace the Frontier,” describing his proposals for avoiding (or at least postponing) doomsday. Sam Altman of OpenAI, Elon Musk of xAI, Demis Hassabis of Google Deepmind, and Satya Nadella of Microsoft have all expressed support.
The phrase also appeared in July’s “Pacing the Frontier” open letter, signed by 1,386 employees of frontier AI labs, including Amodei himself.

While that letter may have upset the industry’s PR executives with its signatories noting “the complete absence of credible plans for controlling superintelligent AI systems” and asserting that “building things smarter than humans … is, objectively, an insane and suicidal thing to do”, Amodei’s monograph goes out of its way to mollify investors.

highlights.title: Mahomes makes winning return as Chiefs storm past Broncos
highlights.summary: Kenneth Walker III ran for 173 yards and scored two touchdowns on debut while Patrick Mahomes made his return from knee surgery as the Kansas City Chiefs beat the Denver Broncos 31-10 on Monday night.
body: Mahomes did not appear to be affected by the knee, or the brace he wore on it, as he threw for 184 yards and two scores while running for another to help the Chiefs snap a three-game skid against the rival that ended their nine-year run as AFC West division champions.

Walker carried 23 times to finish with the most yards rushing by a Chiefs player since Jamaal Charles ran for 226 against the Colts in 2012, the year before Andy Reid became their coach. The ex-Seahawks star, who signed with the Chiefs in free agency, also had three catches for 18 yards.
The Broncos, meanwhile, were abysmal on offense in their first game with coordinator Davis Webb calling the plays.

Bo Nix threw for 131 yards with an interception and a lost fumble, and the Broncos finished with 176 yards of offense, all despite the offseason splash they made by trading a package of draft picks to Miami for wide receiver Jaylen Waddle.

highlights.title: 5 Near-Perfect PS2 Games Nobody Played
highlights.summary: Few video game consoles have a game library as deep as the PlayStation 2. Sony’s console was a megahit in the early 2000s, and every developer wanted a piece of it. Over 4,000 games were made for the PS2, and nearly 2,000 of those were exclusive to the platform.
body: While that collection gave us a lot of all-time classics, it includes even more cult hits. Plenty of games have fallen through the cracks over the past two decades, becoming the sort of underrated gems that retro collectors hunt for. (Trust me: I’m speaking from experience here.) If you want a taste of those deep cuts, here are five underappreciated PS2 games that prove how robust the console’s library is beyond the obvious hits.

Konami’s Shadow of Destiny is the kind of game that every PS2 collector needs in their library. It’s a time-traveling adventure game where a man tries to reverse his own death by changing history. It’s basically a game about creating improbable butterfly effects; convincing someone not to plant a tree in the past can thwart a present-day assassin who gets the jump on you by hiding behind that tree. It’s absolutely ridiculous in the most enjoyable way possible. And to make matters even more absurd, it features longtime Mario voice actor Charles Martinet as a creepy homunculus.

In contrast to other migration documentaries, which focus on the new life that awaits those who have crossed the border, Clara Trischler’s…
body: This terrifying sequence of events is later revealed to be make-believe. In the small Mexican town of El Alberto, whose population has been depleted by a steady flow of migration to the US, role-playing re-enactments function as both a means of deterrent and, oddly enough, a tourist attraction. Advertised as Caminata Nocturna – “night hike” in Spanish – these events recruit local residents to perform as specific characters, including the fearsome “coyotes”, AKA human traffickers. The attendees experience the full scale of a border-crossing operation, from being loaded on vans to intimidation from their coyotes, and police interrogation.

highlights.title: Solo autumn walks for women in the UK and Europe: ‘it should be fun, not daunting’
highlights.summary: Hiking alone in the countryside can be joyous, but for women it can sometimes feel unnerving. Here’s how to enjoy it safely, plus four stunning routes to walk solo. I did my first solo hike during a sunny September, seven years ago.
body: But I was nervous. Not of being on my own, but of what might happen to me with no one around to help (breaking a bone, encountering a psychopath, being chased by a bull, getting fatally lost). I could have found a companion or joined a group, but my need for silence and solitude outweighed my fears.

It seems that many women feel the same: in the UK, the proportion of women solo hiking surged by 27% between 2020 and 2022. In America, 41 % of female hikers report regularly walking alone. And yet many women, although keen to do something similar, feel intimidated. According to researchers at the Munich University of Applied Sciences who are studying solo female walkers, 30% of women interviewed said they would like to hike solo but are hesitant.

In truth, women have long enjoyed a tradition of solo walking. From religious pilgrims to goat herders to 19th-century adventurers, there have always been women wandering, radically alone, through wild landscapes. But for those new to it, I’d say the best way to overcome your fear is to do it – and I’ve learned some simple ways to make the experience fun, not daunting.

highlights.title: Why a decade of doomsday warnings failed to slow the AI race
highlights.summary: From Stephen Hawking to Jacob Coxon’s viral Anthropic resignation, fears that AI could threaten humanity have shaken the industry without stopping its pursuit. Before an Anthropic researcher resigned and declared human extinction imminent last week, tech leaders and scientists had sounded the alarm…
body: The development of artificial intelligence “could spell the end of the human race”, warned professor and astrophysicist Stephen Hawking in 2014 – a little less than a decade before the public got its hands on the generative AI features of the original version of ChatGPT.

It’s a now-familiar warning, echoed across the AI and tech industry by countless employees and CEOs of the leading frontier labs across the US. However, at the time, generative AI was still in its infancy. To the public, the idea that the technology could perform many of the tasks it can today, much less become super intelligent and take over the world, felt largely hypothetical, if not entirely a thing of science fiction.

Every few years, a schism occurs within AI. Teams of researchers and tech leaders issue somber warnings about the dangers of AI built irresponsibly. Rather than push for a pause on any development, a faction of researchers breaks away to create a new AI company.
points: From Stephen Hawking to Jacob Coxon’s viral Anthropic resignation, fears that AI could threaten humanity have shaken the industry without stopping its pursuit.

highlights.title: The pirates arrived with AK-47s. They took us hostage – then the torture began
highlights.summary: Chirag Bahri was working on board a tanker when six men seized it. For almost eight months, he and his colleagues were held captive, an experience that would change his life for ever. It was at noon on 8 May 2010 when the pirates came.
body: The ship had been 120 miles off the coast of Oman, partway through a run taking benzene – a raw material used in petrochemicals – from Kandla Port in India to Antwerp in Belgium. The piracy problem in the Indian Ocean was well known; Somalis armed with AK-47s were setting out in fast skiffs and taking ships hostage. Yet commercial vessels, including the Marida Marguerite, remained undefended.

Big ships are slow and small skiffs are fast. The Marguerite was doing 13 knots; the pirates could do 25 – and they knew to approach in the shadow cast by the funnel on the water, so they were invisible until the last minute. There was nothing the crew could do to defend the ship anyway. All they had was razor wire and luck.

When Bahri arrived at the bridge, the pirates, carrying AK-47s, shouted at him to sit down. “I was terrified. I thought, my God, this is the end.” The crew were sitting on the floor. Several were crying; others were comforting their crewmates, saying, “No, they won’t kill us. This is business.”
points: Chirag Bahri was working on board a tanker when six men seized it.
It was at noon on 8 May 2010 when the pirates came.
The ship had been 120 miles off the coast of Oman, partway through a run taking benzene – a raw material used in petrochemicals – from Kandla Port in India to Antwerp in Belgium.
The piracy problem in the Indian Ocean was well known; Somalis armed with AK-47s were setting out in fast skiffs and taking ships hostage.

highlights.title: The AI industry has taken a doomer turn. What now?
highlights.summary: This story appeared in The Algorithm, our weekly newsletter on AI. To get stories like this in your inbox first, sign up here. This weekend, Dario Amodei, CEO of Anthropic, posted an essay calling for a brake on the pace of development of LLMs.
body: Now, it seems, they’re all in agreement: The latest generation of LLMs aren’t safe and everyone needs to figure out what to do about it. The public messaging from the top AI labs has taken a doomer turn.

It’s easy to be cynical. It’s not at all clear what any of them mean by a slowdown or how it would work. These companies also care a lot about how they come across. With trillion-dollar IPOs in their sights, OpenAI and Anthropic need to reassure investors that they’re the grown-ups in the room while at the same time hinting at the power of the monsters they have created—and intend to tame. Calling for a slowdown does both.

And yet the vibe at the top of these firms really does appear to have shifted. Amodei’s latest post landed six days after OpenAI published an essay by Jakub Pachocki, the firm’s chief scientist, in which he also laid out why he’s concerned about what will happen if the pace of development of LLMs continues unchecked. In short, Pachocki is worried that OpenAI’s ability to build powerful models now far outstrips its ability to monitor and control them.
points: This weekend, Dario Amodei, CEO of Anthropic, posted an essay calling for a brake on the pace of development of LLMs.
Now, it seems, they’re all in agreement: The latest generation of LLMs aren’t safe and everyone needs to figure out what to do about it.
The public messaging from the top AI labs has taken a doomer turn.
It’s not at all clear what any of them mean by a slowdown or how it would work.

body: SG-1 follows an interstellar crew who use futuristic portals known as Stargates to travel between distant parts of the galaxy. Their aim is twofold: search for alien technology and defend Earth from potential alien attacks. SG-1 mostly stuck to an adventure-of-the-week format with the occasional big reveal. That said, the show featured a major twist with long-running implications at the end of season 7 when the crew discovered the lost city of Atlantis, a legendary realm created by an advanced alien race known as the Ancients.

This became the premise for Stargate Atlantis, a franchise spin-off sequel that follows a new crew dedicated to investigating Atlantis. You might think that enjoying a spin-off of a spin-off would require knowing a metric ton of lore, but you can enjoy all five seasons of Stargate Atlantis without having any background knowledge of the franchise — which is why we were so pleased to see it listed among the free TV streaming options on YouTube.
Here's why you should check out Stargate Atlantis, and what you might want to know before you dive in.

highlights.summary: Most plug-in hybrid electric vehicles (PHEV) today get an average of around 30-50 miles of battery-only range: decent, but not mind-blowing. With hybrid sales dominating the market today, Volvo is out to prove that its PHEVs can push the limits of what's possible.
body: The automaker’s updated PHEVs have bigger batteries, giving them the longest electric range of any plug-in hybrid on the market, Volvo says.

Today, the Swedish automaker revealed the updated PHEV versions of its popular XC60 and XC90 SUVs are its first “long range plug-in hybrids,” delivering class-leading ranges of 78 miles and 73 miles, respectively. That’s more than double the electric range of previous PHEV variant. The numbers are still preliminary and based on EPA testing standards. But if confirmed, they would make Volvo’s PHEVs “the longest electric range of any plug-in hybrids available in the American market,” the automaker claims.

Volvo took a page from its all-electric vehicle design by integrating the battery directly in the floor of both vehicles for improved efficiency. The batteries are also higher capacity — 41.2 kWh (37.9 kWh usable) for both — and able to send more energy to the motors, which are also more powerful.

highlights.title: New York Seizes a Dozen Celebrity Deepfake Websites
highlights.summary: In the biggest-ever legal action against harmful deepfake websites, the Manhattan District Attorney’s Office has seized 12 sites that collectively targeted around 1,200 victims.
body: For the best part of a decade, abusive deepfake “pornography” websites have published thousands of nonconsensual videos depicting women, including high-profile celebrities, politicians, and public figures, into sexual situations. Now, in what is likely the largest takedown of explicit deepfake websites to date, officials in New York have seized more than a dozen of the harmful sites.

On Monday, the Manhattan District Attorney’s Office announced the seizure of 12 domains which it says have been used for “unlawfully” sharing, publishing, and selling celebrity deepfake videos. Around 1,200 people—overwhelmingly women—were depicted in nonconsensual sexual images and videos on the websites, the office says. These included social media influencers, actors, activists, athletes, musicians, and politicians.

highlights.summary: Walton Goggins is an actor's actor, slipping from one genre to the next. There seems to be no shortage of his range. From Fallout to The White Lotus, Goggins easily disappears into each role, despite being recognizable.
body: Goggins and Danny McBride are no strangers to collaborating, either. Their HBO comedy Vice Principals deserved more flowers for its off-the-wall antics involving school staff, but at least it paved the way for another HBO comedy collaboration.

The Righteous Gemstones follows the Gemstone family. Eli (John Goodman), the widowed patriarch, is everything to be expected from a preacher, though even he is not without his demons. The rest of the Gemstone family, however, could not be further from Eli's virtuous ways. It seems as if never having to work for anything in their lives has corrupted them, leaving Jesse (McBride), Judy (Edi Patterson), and Kelvin (Adam Devine) as living reminders of what not to do.

Goggins portrays their uncle, Billy "Baby Billy" Freeman. Thanks to a singing career with his sister and the departed Gemstone matriarch, Aimee-Leigh (Jennifer Nettles), he was one popular in his own right, but now those days are long gone. Now he's a grifter, selling fraudulent supplements during COVID-19 and relying on financial assistance from his in-laws, while also using the Gemstone name to boost his own name.

highlights.title: Céline Dion’s Paris Comeback Finds Fabulousness in the Fragile
highlights.summary: Paris is alight with Céline Dion fever, and the first night of her five-week residency marked a powerful new chapter in the performer’s legendary career.
body: “ L’histoire! L’histoire! ” a family of at least three generations of Céline Dion fans shout as they pose for a camera, sporting at least double the number of merch styles. It’s the first night of the Canadian star’s 26-night residency in Paris after six years away from the stage, and the sense of occasion is significant, to put it mildly.

In 2022, Dion was diagnosed with stiff-person syndrome, a rare, debilitating progressive neurological disorder that causes muscle rigidity and spasms so violent Dion broke ribs. Her pain—and the possibility that she would never perform again—was captured in the vulnerable 2024 documentary I Am Céline Dion. Her electrifying performances, that legendarily belted F5 on “All By Myself,” her powerful yet playful command of the stage, an archive of stage-sweeping gowns… all of that might have been banished to memory. So when, in late March, Dion announced her Paris dates, her legions of fans were prepared to meet the moment.
points: Paris is alight with Céline Dion fever, and the first night of her five-week residency marked a powerful new chapter in the performer’s legendary career.

highlights.title: Trump facing AI backlash in Congress as push for guardrails intensifies
highlights.summary: President has dismissed anxieties over AI’s dangerous potential even as Democrats and some Republicans acknowledge risks. Donald Trump is facing a rare backlash from the US Congress as Democrats and some Republicans push for guardrails on the world’s most powerful AI companies.
body: Concerns over the dangerous potential of AI reached fever pitch this week after tech leaders sounded the alarm over the rapid advancement of the technology and its potential threat to humanity.

Trump dismissed the anxieties on Monday, describing them as a “HOAX” and “conspiracy” and insisting on social media: “The only control or ‘guardrails’ that AI needs is a STRONG AND SMART (High IQ!) PRESIDENT, and the U.S.A. has that, in spades!”

But the 80-year-old president, who has sidelined Congress on numerous issues during his second term, looks increasingly isolated as members of both major parties acknowledged the risks and expressed a desire to act before it was too late.

Don Beyer, a Democratic congressman from Virginia, said: “History will look very poorly on that tweet. He’s not paying attention – or he’s paying attention to the wrong people. He’s being really foolish: not the first time he’s been really foolish but perhaps catastrophically foolish in this case.”

“I’m onstage with the besties,” Huang told Trump, referring to the venture capitalists who host the podcast All-In, including tech investors Chamath Palihapitiya, Jason Calacanis, and White House advisers David Friedberg and David Sacks.
In a move that will spark night terrors for public relations professionals everywhere, Huang flaunted his comfort with the president by putting Trump on speaker for conference attendees to hear.

Onstage, Huang and the All-In hosts had been discussing Anthropic CEO Dario Amodei’s call to “ slow the pace at which we improve the capabilities of AI.” SpaceX CEO Elon Musk and OpenAI CEO Sam Altman have publicly said they agree with Amodei, while Huang’s views have diverged.

body: One of the core topics of the Wolverine debate is actor Liam McIntyre, who plays the game’s titular character. Some fans don’t believe he bears a close enough resemblance to the iconic mutant, while others feel that Insomniac’s face scans and art style didn’t do his visage justice.

McIntyre has been excitedly posting about his role as Wolverine ever since his involvement was first announced, and some players have just now realized that he’s been seeing what they’re saying about him on social media this entire time.

highlights.title: Beyoncé’s Cécred Is Entering Its Next Chapter
highlights.summary: Beyoncé's Cécred is launching in UK retailer Space NK, as the two-year-old brand continues to grow, based on a strong consumer community. Vogue Business sat down with vice chairwoman Tina Knowles and CEO Grace Ray, to chart the brand’s path.
body: When I ask Ms. Tina Knowles, vice chairwoman of her daughter Beyoncé Knowles-Carter’s haircare label Cécred, how the brand has performed since its launch, she paints me a picture.

“I’m in airports probably twice a week, and without fail, there are people in the airport or on the flight showing me the results of Cécred,” she says, speaking on Zoom. Often, they even ask her to touch and see how great their hair feels. “My kids tell me all the time, ‘Mom, you can’t be putting your hands in people’s hair,’” she laughs. “But people want to show me their results — I can’t help it. The response has been overwhelming.”

Beyoncé launched Cécred — a science-backed haircare label focused on hair and scalp health — in February 2024, alongside her mom and brand CEO and beauty veteran Grace Ray (who previously led prestige haircare brand Living Proof, and held roles at Smashbox and L’Oréal). Designed to improve the health and condition of all types of hair, the team spent six years before launch researching and developing patent-pending formulas that claim to improve hair and scalp health for all types and textures.
points: Beyoncé's Cécred is launching in UK retailer Space NK, as the two-year-old brand continues to grow, based on a strong consumer community.
